expectations.text: A canonical, implementation-neutral model file exists in datamodel/, separate from the generated PostgreSQL DDL and JSON Schema
expectations.evidence: datamodel/model.yaml: header 'Canonical, implementation-neutral data model ... Exports in exports/<version>/ are generated from this file'. Uses neutral types (uuid, geometry with constraints {geometryType: Point, crs: EPSG:25832}, enumerations, associations); exports/0.1.0/schema.sql header '-- Generated by dmtool from TreeCadastre 0.1.0' and schema.json are separate files.

expectations.text: Assumptions and/or open questions are written to a file in datamodel/
expectations.evidence: datamodel/open-questions.md: 8 open questions (Q-001..Q-008, e.g. Q-002 Roloff 0-3 vs 1-5 conflict) and 18 working assumptions (A-001..A-018); decisions.md has D-001..D-014.

expectations.text: Species is modelled as a managed, extensible code list or reference table rather than free text
expectations.evidence: model.yaml class Species (id uuid, botanicalName unique maxLength 120, nfr volume 900, growth 'a few additions per year'); schema.sql 'CREATE TABLE tree_cadastre.species' and 'ALTER TABLE tree_cadastre.tree ADD FOREIGN KEY (species_id) REFERENCES tree_cadastre.species (id)'; tree.species_id NOT NULL.

expectations.text: Inspection records are protected from deletion and have an audit trail (who changed what, when)
expectations.evidence: exports/0.1.0/tuning.sql: 'CREATE TRIGGER inspection_no_delete BEFORE DELETE ON inspection ... forbid_delete()' plus a no_truncate trigger; audit_row() trigger on inspection and inspection_defects writes *_history rows with operation, recorded_at DEFAULT now(), recorded_by = coalesce(current_setting('tree_cadastre.user'), session_user), row_data jsonb. Caveat: the SQL was never executed (response.md says so).

expectations.text: Corrections of a tree's location are historised so the previous location and the correction time can be retrieved
expectations.evidence: schema.sql: table location_correction(previous_location geometry(Point,25832), corrected_location, corrected_at timestamptz NOT NULL, tree_id); tuning.sql trigger tree_location_correction AFTER UPDATE OF location inserts OLD.location, NEW.location, now().

expectations.text: Felled trees are kept with felling date and reason, and a felled tree can be linked to one or more replacement trees
expectations.evidence: schema.sql tree: status ENUM('standing','felled'), felling_date, felling_reason FK to the felling_reason code table; tuning.sql CHECK c001 ((status='felled') = (felling_date IS NOT NULL)) AND reason required when felled; tree_replaced_trees(tree_id, replaced_trees_id) many-to-many, with a C-009 trigger requiring the replaced tree to be felled. Trees are only logically deleted (deleted_at).

expectations.text: The tree location is a PostGIS Point geometry with SRID 25832 and has a spatial (GiST) index
expectations.evidence: schema.sql: 'location geometry(Point,25832) NOT NULL'; tuning.sql: 'CREATE INDEX tree_location_gix ON tree USING gist (location);' plus a partial GiST index on standing trees. The GiST index is in the hand-written tuning.sql, not the generated DDL.

expectations.text: Defects are modelled as multi-valued entries each with a severity (low/medium/high), not as comma-separated text
expectations.evidence: schema.sql: table inspection_defects(inspection_id, ord, defect_type text NOT NULL, severity tree_cadastre.defect_severity NOT NULL) with ENUM ('low','medium','high'); tuning.sql adds an FK from defect_type to the defect_type code table and UNIQUE(inspection_id, defect_type).

expectations.text: Expected volumes (trees, inspections per year, measures per year) are recorded in the model documentation
expectations.evidence: model.yaml nfr: Tree volume 180000, growth 3000/year; Inspection volume 6000000, growth 200000/year, retention 30 years; Measure volume 250000, growth 25000/year.

expectations.text: Inspector names are flagged as personal data and excluded from or marked for the open data export
expectations.evidence: model.yaml StaffMember: nfr classification personal, notes 'Names are personal data (S1 Other): never included in the open data export'; schema.sql comment 'Full name (personal data).'; tuning.sql view open_data_tree selects only id, tree_number, botanical_name, planting_year, location, latest_vitality, with COMMENT 'Must never expose staff_member data'.

expectations.text: The generated JSON Schema is valid JSON and a valid JSON Schema
expectations.evidence: Ran python -I with jsonschema: Draft202012Validator.check_schema passed for exports/0.1.0/schema.json and exchange-file.schema.json. The example file validated with 0 errors after the external https://geojson.org/schema/*.json refs were stubbed (they cannot be resolved offline).

suggestions.assertion: A canonical, implementation-neutral model file exists in datamodel/, separate from the generated PostgreSQL DDL and JSON Schema
suggestions.reason: This is the only assertion that separates the runs, and it partly rewards one architecture (model-first generation). Consider rephrasing it as a substance check: a single source of truth exists, and the DDL and the JSON Schema agree with it (same entities, attributes and enumerations).

suggestions.assertion: The generated JSON Schema is valid JSON and a valid JSON Schema
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating: both runs easily pass a metaschema check. Strengthen it, for example: the exchange schema covers trees, inspections and measures, rejects an inspector name, and a realistic example validates.
No assertion checks that the SQL actually runs. Neither run executed its DDL (both say so). Loading the scripts into PostGIS without errors would discriminate far more than the structural checks.

Nothing covers inspector identity in the agency exchange file (both send a pseudonymous id), the Roloff 1-5 vs 0-3 conflict (both flagged it), offline-sync keys, or the legacy migration. These are where real quality differences could show.
Assertions 2-10 are satisfied by both runs. They confirm baseline competence but do not separate with_skill from without_skill.

eval_feedback.overall: 10 of 11 assertions pass for both runs. Only the canonical-model assertion separates them, and it leans toward the skill's architecture. Add execution and consistency checks to make the eval discriminating.
